headline: The warehouse-robot start-up Ultra has raised $62 million and deepened its partnership with the AI company Physical Intelligence.
score_reason: Modest round, but a clear example of robots being rented to warehouses; key figures are company claims.
importance_line: Shows warehouse robots being rented by the month instead of bought, which matters to logistics companies; the order count and the claim that Ultra has raised prices are the company's own, and revenue was not disclosed.
summary: Fortune reports that Ultra, a Brooklyn company that leases robots that pack goods to warehouses for a monthly fee, has raised $62 million, made up of a $50 million Series A led by Framework Ventures and an earlier $12 million seed round, and is deepening its partnership with Physical Intelligence, a $5.6 billion AI company that supplies the software the robots learn from. According to Ultra, its robots have packed more than half a million orders, and its customers pay an up-front installation fee and then a monthly support fee rather than buying the machines.
notes: machine_action true because the article says installed robots are packing orders in warehouses (company claim); the story is mainly a funding round, so category stays MKT.
